items.quote: Relations
A relation of set of X to the set of Y.
items.text: What you'll learn: A relation of set of X to the set of Y. A relation from a set on it self.

items.quote: Key terms Relation.
In the festival "Reading for All", five students represent
items.text: Think and Discuss intro: In the festival "Reading for All", five students represent the set of X = {a, b, c, d, e} went to the school library to read some books which are represented by the set Y = [science, literature, culture and history] student A read a book in science and a book in culture, student b read a book in histroy, student c read a literary book, pupil e read a book of the historical books, but student d didn't read any of these books.
items.notes: Y printed with '[' and closing ']' rather than braces; possible misprint.

items.quote: Reading for all
items.caption: Picture of people holding up books, labelled 'Reading for all' (decorative-ish illustration).

items.quote: Write the previous statements in the form of ordered pairs from
items.text: Write the previous statements in the form of ordered pairs from X to Y.

items.quote: Represent a set of the ordered pairs in the form of an arrow
items.text: Represent a set of the ordered pairs in the form of an arrow diagram.

items.quote: The expression " read" connects some of the elements of the set
items.claim: The expression "read" connects some elements of set X with elements of set Y and determines a relation between X and Y, denoted by the symbol R. It can be represented by an arrow diagram, drawing an arrow from the student to the type of books he reads.

items.quote: as shown in the opposite figure
items.caption: Arrow diagram from X={a,b,c,d,e} to Y={Science, art, culture, history}. Arrows: a→Science, a→culture, b→history, c→culture(?), e→history; d has no arrow. Y lists 'art' where text says literature.
items.notes: Arrows read from small figure; verify. Label 'art' vs text 'literature'.

items.quote: This set of ordered pairs are called the relation R.
items.claim: The set of ordered pairs {(a, Science), (a, Culture), (b, Histrory), (c, Literature), (e, History)} expresses the relation from X to Y and is called the relation R.

misprints.notes: spelling; also closing '}' after ')' brackets mismatch

items.quote: Is R a subset from the cartesian product X × Z?
items.text: Is R a subset from the cartesian product $X \times Z$?

misprints.notes: R is a relation from X to Y

items.quote: If X = {-1, 1, 2}, Y = {2, 4, 6, 8}, and R is a relation
items.stem: If $X=\{-1,1,2\}$, $Y=\{2,4,6,8\}$, and R is a relation from X to Y where a R b means: «b = 2a + 4», for each $a\in X$, $b\in Y$. Write and represent R once in an arrow diagram and another by a cartesian diagram.

items.quote: Arrow diagram
items.caption: Arrow diagram from X to Y: X = {-1, 1, 2}, Y = {2, 4, 6, 8}; arrows -1→2, 1→6, 2→8.

items.quote: Graph digram
items.caption: Graph diagram with X axis marks -1, 1, 2 and Y axis marks 2, 4, 6, 8; points plotted at (-1, 2), (1, 6), (2, 8).

items.quote: The relation from X to Y where X, Y are two non-empty sets
items.claim: A relation from X to Y, where X and Y are two non-empty sets, connects some or all elements of X with some or all elements of Y.

items.quote: X × Y is the set of ordered pairs where the first projection
items.claim: X × Y is the set of ordered pairs where the first projection in each pair belongs to X and the second projection belongs to Y.

items.quote: If R is a relation from X to Y , then R ⊂ X × Y
items.claim: If R is a relation from X to Y, then R is a subset of X × Y.

items.quote: The relation from a set to itself
items.text: The relation from a set to itself

items.quote: If R is a relation from a set X to X (itself) then R is called a relation
items.claim: If R is a relation from a set X to X (itself), then R is called a relation on X, and R ⊂ X × X.

items.quote: If X = {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2} and R is a given relation on X
items.stem: If $X=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ and R is a given relation on X where a R b means: «The number a is the additive inverse of the number b» for each of a, b ∈ X. Write the relation R and represent it by an arrow diagram and also by cartesian diagram.

items.quote: Arrow diagram
items.caption: Arrow diagram of R on X: number line with arcs linking -2↔2, -1↔1 and a loop at 0; also an oval with X = {-2,-1,0,1,2} showing a loop on 0 and double arrows between -1 and 1, -2 and 2.

items.quote: Cartesian Diagram
items.caption: Cartesian diagram with both axes marked -2 to 2; points plotted at (-2, 2), (-1, 1), (0, 0), (1, -1), (2, -2).

learning_objectives.label: Write relations as ordered pairs
learning_objectives.description: Write a relation from a set X to a set Y as a set of ordered pairs, using the rule connecting a and b (e.g. b = 2a + 4, or 'a is a digit of b').

learning_objectives.label: Represent relations by diagrams
learning_objectives.description: Represent a relation by an arrow diagram and by a cartesian diagram.

learning_objectives.label: Relations as subsets of X × Y
learning_objectives.description: Determine whether a relation is a subset of the cartesian product X × Y, decide which ordered pairs satisfy the stated relation, and identify a relation on a set X as R ⊂ X × X.
